items.body:
At the moment, there's no proper way to detect the click on "done" in a virtual keyboard. All we receive is a "blur" event on the text field, which is indistinguishable from other "blur" causes.

We may be able to detect this by checking the new focus target. If it's `<body>` then the user most likely clicked "done" on the virtual keyboard. That is because iOS doesn't blur text fields when the user taps on random parts of the page. The only ways to blur are: click "done" or click some other focusable element (e.g. another text field).

items.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create repro --platforms web` and replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below.
2. `flutter run -d chrome` (or `flutter build web` and serve `build/web`). Semantics is turned on by `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`. Clicking the "Enable accessibility" placeholder or running a screen reader does the same; both were tried, with the same result.
3. Click the text field (it holds `hello`) and type ` world`.
4. Scroll the list down with the mouse wheel until the text field is off-screen, then scroll back up.

### Expected results

The field still shows `hello world`, and `controller.text` (printed at the bottom) is `hello world`. With semantics off, that is what happens.

### Actual results

The field is empty and `controller.text` is `""`. The framework received an editing-state update with empty text, as if the user had deleted everything. The field is still focused, and the next keystroke continues from the empty value.

Any change that removes a focused text field's semantics node for one semantics update and brings it back in a later one does the same. Two other triggers we hit:

- **A layout change on resize.** In our app, a multi-pane layout switches to a single pane, and the editing pane's semantics subtree is detached for one frame.
- **`ExcludeSemantics` toggled on for one frame.**

The field's `State`, controller and focus all survive in every case. Only the engine's DOM `<input>` is re-created.

### Code sample

```dart
// Flutter web, semantics enabled: a focused TextField loses its text when its
// semantics node leaves the tree and comes back. Here: the field is scrolled
// out of view (a focused EditableText keeps itself alive off-screen) and back.
//
//   flutter run -d chrome
//
// 1. Click the field (it holds "hello"), optionally type.
// 2. Scroll the list down with the mouse wheel until the field is off-screen.
// 3. Scroll back up: the field is empty, and so is controller.text below.
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/semantics.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Repro()));
  // What a screen reader, or clicking "Enable accessibility", does.
  SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics();
}

class Repro extends StatefulWidget {
  const Repro({super.key});

  @override
  State<Repro> createState() => _ReproState();
}

class _ReproState extends State<Repro> {
  final _controller = TextEditingController(text: 'hello');

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Scaffold(
      body: ListView(
        children: [
          Padding(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
            child: TextField(controller: _controller),
          ),
          for (var i = 0; i < 100; i++) ListTile(title: Text('Row $i')),
        ],
      ),
      bottomNavigationBar: ValueListenableBuilder(
        valueListenable: _controller,
        builder: (context, value, _) => Padding(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
          child: Text('controller.text = "${value.text}"'),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### What happens in the engine

Line references are to 3.47.7 stable. That is framework [`abaf9c5237`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/tree/abaf9c523780a608bd46686fd5e53740a07077f8), whose `web_ui` sources are identical to engine revision `deb287481e` (empty `git diff`). Paths are under `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/`.

What is **proven** comes from three sources:

- the source, read at the lines given;
- a DOM trace: `focusin`, `focusout` and `selectionchange` listeners on `document` in the capture phase, a `MutationObserver` on `<body>`, and an element-identity check;
- the controller's own listener, logging each change.

What is **inferred** is marked as such.

1. While scrolled away, the field's `EditableText` is kept alive because it has focus (`wantKeepAlive => widget.focusNode.hasFocus`, `packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/editable_text.dart:2638`). Its semantics node is no longer part of the semantics tree.
   - Trace: the field's `flt-semantics` host is removed from the DOM.
   - Trace: the controller is unchanged while away.
   - The framework keeps focus and keeps the text-input connection open. _Inferred_ from the next steps: on return the engine sees `hasFocus` and activates the new field, and `HybridTextEditing.isEditing` is still true.
2. **Removal update.** The detached node is permanently removed in `_finalizeTree`, which calls `removal.dispose()` ([semantics/semantics.dart#L3187](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/abaf9c523780a608bd46686fd5e53740a07077f8/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/semantics.dart#L3187)).
   - `SemanticsObject.dispose()` calls `safeRemoveSync(element)` (`semantics.dart:2716`), which moves DOM focus to the view root. Trace: `focusout` on the `<input>`, then `focusin` on `FLUTTER-VIEW`.
   - Both the `<input>`'s `blur` listener ([semantics/text_field.dart#L306-L311](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/abaf9c523780a608bd46686fd5e53740a07077f8/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/semantics/text_field.dart#L306-L311)) and `SemanticTextField.dispose()` (`text_field.dart:401-405`) call `SemanticsTextEditingStrategy.deactivate(this)`.
   - `deactivate` leads to `disable()` (`text_field.dart:100-121`), which sets **`lastEditingState = null`** (`text_field.dart:116`) and drops `domElement`.
   - The framework is not told anything: no `onConnectionClosed`, and `isEditing` stays true.
3. **Re-add update.** The node comes back under the same id. The engine has already disposed its `SemanticsObject`, so it builds a new one, and `_updateRole` creates a new `SemanticTextField` (`semantics.dart:2379`).
   - Its constructor creates a **new, empty** `<input>` (`text_field.dart:233-235`, `253-256`). Nothing ever copies `semanticsObject.value` into it ([#194548](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/194548)).
   - Trace: the `<input>` after the round trip is a different element from the one before, and its `value` is `""`.
   - `update()` sees `semanticsObject.hasFocus` and calls `activate(this)` (`text_field.dart:323-330`). That calls `DefaultTextEditingStrategy.enable()` ([text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1759-L1782](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/abaf9c523780a608bd46686fd5e53740a07077f8/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/text_editing/text_editing.dart#L1759-L1782)).
   - In `enable()`, `if (lastEditingState != null) setEditingState(...)` (`text_editing.dart:1770`) is skipped, because step 2 nulled it. The framework does not re-send `TextInput.setEditingState`, because from its side the connection never closed.
   - `moveFocusToActiveDomElement()` then focuses the empty element. Trace: `focusin` on the new `<input>` with `value=""`.
4. Chrome fires `selectionchange` for the newly focused input (trace: `selectionchange` on the new `<input>`, `value=""`).
   - The strategy's `document` `selectionchange` subscription (`text_field.dart:137`) runs `handleChange()` (`text_editing.dart:1617-1642`).
   - `handleChange()` builds `EditingState(text: '', base: 0, extent: 0)` from the DOM. That differs from `lastEditingState` (null), so it calls `onChange`.
   - `onChange` sends `channel.updateEditingState` (`text_editing.dart:2623`) to `TextInputClient.updateEditingState` (`packages/flutter/lib/src/services/text_input.dart:2260`), then to `EditableText.updateEditingValue` (`editable_text.dart:3653`).
   - Result: the controller's text becomes `""` (the controller log shows the `""` entry).

Proof that step 4 is what delivers the empty value: with a capturing `selectionchange` listener on `window` that stops propagation, the controller kept its text through the round trip. But the first input event afterwards (value set to `4` on the now-empty `<input>`, plus an `input` event) made the controller `"4"`. **Suppressing the event only postpones the loss.** The root cause is steps 2–3: an empty element, and no `lastEditingState` to restore, while the framework believes the connection is intact.

The same sequence was also checked against master `84a33147ed` (3.50.0-1.0.pre-115) by reading the source:

- [#192963](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/192963) added a `blur` guard (`if (owner.phase != idle && hasFocus) return;`, `text_field.dart:418` on master).
- `SemanticTextField.dispose()` still calls `deactivate` (`:529`), and `disable()` still nulls `lastEditingState` (`:163`).
- `enable()` still restores only a non-null state (`text_editing.dart:1993`), and the new element is still empty (`:336`).

**The minimal repro reproduces on that master build too.**

### Variants tried

Chrome 154 on Linux. Release builds unless noted. "Lost" means the controller received `""`.

| Variant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Code sample above, 3.47.7 stable, trusted click + trusted typing (CDP), wheel scroll away and back | **lost** |
| Code sample above, master `84a33147ed` | **lost** |
| Focused field with `ExcludeSemantics(excluding: true)` for exactly one frame (placeholder-enabled semantics) | **lost** |
| Same, triggered by a viewport width change (1200 → 380 via device-metrics override) | **lost** |
| Same, focused but never typed into (initial controller text) | **lost** |
| Same, `flutter build web --profile` | **lost** |
| Same, field edited and then unfocused before the one-frame exclusion | kept: the `<input>` is still re-created empty, but no edit is sent |
| Same, semantics off | kept |
| `ListView` scroll away and back, semantics off | kept |
| Lone focused `TextField`, width change 500 → 380 | kept: same semantics node, same `<input>` |
| Field moved between `Row` and `Column` under a `GlobalKey` on a width change | kept: same semantics node |
| Field with an `OverlayPortal` popup shown beside it, width change 1200 → 380 | kept |

Not tried: debug (DDC) build, `--wasm`, Firefox, Safari, Windows, macOS, a real screen reader (NVDA, VoiceOver). The wheel events in the scroll variant were dispatched from JS on `flt-glass-pane`; the click and typing were trusted CDP input.

### Possible directions

Suggestions only, not tested.

- **Keep the editing state across a deactivate while the framework connection is still open.** When `HybridTextEditing.isEditing` is true, re-activation of a new element for the same client would re-apply the last state, as `enable()` already does when `lastEditingState` is non-null.
- **Seed a new semantics `<input>` with `semanticsObject.value` and its text selection** (the [#194548](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/194548) fix). This alone keeps the text. It may still send a selection change if the seeded selection differs from the framework's.
- **Don't report the DOM state as a user edit when nothing changed it.** In `handleChange`, with no `lastEditingState`, the first state read is the element's initial state, not an edit.

items.body:
Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/189744

**Reland of #190014, reverted in #190926.**

Cause: three of the new tests dispatch a real input.blur(), but desktop Safari uses SafariDesktopTextEditingStrategy, which does not subscribe to blur, so handleBlur never ran. Real iOS does subscribe, so the fix itself was unaffected.

Delta: one test-only commit adding skip: isSafari to those three tests. No production change.

**Problem**
On iOS 27, long-press-dragging the selection caret in a Web TextField dismisses the keyboard mid-gesture. WebKit transiently blurs the hidden input with a null relatedTarget while the document keeps focus, then refocuses it a frame later,and the engine reacted to that blink on two listeners that each tore the input down. A plain input ignores the same blur, so the cause is Flutter's reaction, not a WebKit limitation.

**Fix**
On iOS both listeners now defer their teardown by 100ms and cancel it if the input refocuses, mirroring the existing https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/155265 deferred close. Done and tap-away never refocus so they still close, and the deferral is narrowed to the exact drag signature so every other focus transition is unaffected.

**Demo**
Before: https://flutter-demo-52-before.web.app/ (keyboard dismisses mid caret drag)
After: https://flutter-demo-52-after.web.app/ (keyboard stays up)

Repro on iOS 27 Safari: tap the field to raise the keyboard, then long-press and drag the selection caret. Before dismisses; after stays up. Done and tap-away still dismiss.

<!--

To learn more about code review, see our documentation on Tree Hygiene: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/docs/contributing/Tree-hygiene.md

<!--
Thanks for filing a pull request!
Reviewers are typically assigned within a week of filing a request.
To learn more about code review, see our documentation on Tree Hygiene: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/docs/contributing/Tree-hygiene.md
-->

## What this changes

On the web a password manager could not fill a login form as a pair. Which field arrived depended on which field the manager was invoked from, and in several combinations nothing arrived at all. That is true of shipped builds too, not just of this branch's starting point.

Flutter paints text on canvas and synthesises hidden `<input>` proxies so managers and the browser have something to work with. Those proxies did not satisfy what managers actually check before filling a field. Three causes, each found by reading what the managers check and measuring the live DOM against it:

- **Non focused proxies were zero sized.** `EngineAutofillForm` styled them with `shouldHideElement: !_isWebKit`, so outside WebKit every field of a form except the focused one was `width: 0; height: 0`. A manager will not treat an input that small as a real field (Bitwarden wants 10x10, Proton Pass 30x15), and it confirms the field by hit testing its own centre point and checking it gets that field back, which a zero sized box also fails. So only the focused field was ever a candidate and a login form could not be filled as a pair. The proxies now keep a real size, floored with `min-width`/`min-height` because the framework geometry can itself report a pixel, and the default action of their pointer input is suppressed, so a tap on an invisible field does not move the browser's focus to it. The tap still reaches the app.
- **Closing a connection hid the field the manager was invoked from.** `disable()` parked that field's proxy off screen and zero sized, and a manager's menu taking focus is what closes the connection, so the field being parked was the field the user was in. Invoked from the email field it hid the email field and filled the password; invoked from the password field it hid the password and filled only the email. The shrink also outlives the moment: at least one manager memoises its fillability verdict per element, and these elements are reused for the life of the form, so a single measurement taken while the field was zero sized wrote it off for good. Position is not part of that verdict, so the proxy is moved but keeps its size.
- **The connection was torn down between every field of a single fill.** A manager fills one field at a time, blurring each before focusing the next. That blur lands on `<body>` with no `relatedTarget`, which was reported as the whole view losing focus, so the framework dropped its focus, closed the connection, and rebuilt it when focus returned a moment later. Managers that check their own state between fields lost the rest of the form in that gap. A blur to nothing from a field of a multi-field autofill form (the engine marks that form with a class) now waits before that is reported, and a focus arriving back in the view cancels it. Everything else, including a blur from any other form or to a known element outside the view, is reported at once, unchanged. The wait is on a pair of browser events, a `focusout` and the `focusin` after it, about a millisecond apart. It is not a timer waiting on a manager. It shares its timer and `kTransientBlurSettleDelay` with the iOS caret drag deferral from #190942.

On the first of those, #187108 already established that WebKit refuses to autofill a zero sized input and kept a real size there for that reason. What this adds is that the same holds on every engine once a third party manager rather than the browser is doing the filling: Bitwarden and Proton Pass each apply their own minimum size before they will treat an input as a field. So `_isWebKit` being false on Chrome and Firefox is not the same thing as those engines tolerating a zero sized field. Pointer events follow `_isWebKit` at every proxy site, as #187108 does. Semantics mode keeps the #187108 styling: there the non-focused fields stay hidden off WebKit.

To present a login form a manager can pair, the non focused proxies are stacked under the focused field with `position: fixed`. When the form goes dormant the fields the clustering pinned are parked off screen, above the managers' size floor, and every field leaves the tab order, so nothing of a dismissed form stays hit testable or reachable with Tab. A form that goes dormant while focus is away for a fill (a manager's menu or popup took it) keeps its fields in place until the fill is over, that is the next real tap on the page or the window getting the focus back, because a manager only fills a field that hit tests back to itself.

A pointer event on a non focused proxy, which is hit testable now, is positioned like any other element rather than through the focused field's geometry.

The result is that Bitwarden, Proton Pass and Chrome's own manager each fill both fields, from either field, including after clearing a field by hand and filling again.

Two things follow from the same invariant, that what a manager reads from the DOM has to be what the framework holds. Clearing a field by hand now reaches the proxy, so a manager stops offering to save a password that has already been deleted; previously the proxy kept the last character and the prompt never went away. And a reused proxy no longer serves the previous connection's value to the next manager that reads it.

## Accessibility

Giving the proxies a real size makes them reachable in ways a zero sized element was not, so this is handled explicitly.

Non focused proxies are now set to `tabindex="-1"` (upstream left freshly built proxies in the tab order), and parked ones too, so Tab does not land on an invisible password box; only the focused proxy is in the tab order. With semantics on they are marked `aria-hidden="true"`, which upstream did not do: the field then has a real semantics node and the proxy is a duplicate.

With semantics off the attribute is deliberately not set on the fields. Proton Pass rejects an `aria-hidden` input before it even measures it, so setting it unconditionally puts back the same class of bug this PR fixes, and with semantics off the proxy is the only representation of that field in the DOM, so hiding it hides nothing the user could reach another way.

The form's submit button is `aria-hidden` unconditionally. It is plumbing that only `saveForms` ever clicks, and with semantics off it was what made the invisible proxies read as a complete login form in VoiceOver's form controls rotor.

Google Password Manager's auto submit on mobile is deliberately not addressed here. Separate behaviour, separate discussion, follow up.

## Tested

Demos, the same app built twice, plus a plain HTML login form as a reference for how a manager behaves when Flutter is not involved. The app prints each controller's value on screen, so it is visible whether what the manager wrote reached the Flutter side or only the hidden input.

- Before: https://flutter-autofill-190126.web.app/before/
- After: https://flutter-autofill-190126.web.app/after/
- Plain HTML: https://flutter-autofill-190126.web.app/control/
- Demo source: https://flutter-autofill-190126.web.app/repro/main.dart

Verified against the real extensions in Chrome and Firefox: Bitwarden, Proton Pass and Chrome's own password manager, invoked from each field, and after emptying a field by hand.

`text_editing_test.dart`, `view_focus_binding_test.dart`, `event_position_helper_test.dart` and the semantics text field tests pass on Chrome (dart2js and dart2wasm) and Firefox.

- `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/test/engine/text_editing_test.dart`: 14 added, 1 removed. The removed one is `hidden autofill elements should have a width and height of 0 on non-Safari browsers`, which asserted the behaviour the first cause above changes. It is replaced by `non-focused autofill fields are discoverable and hit-testable on non-Safari browsers`, asserting what the proxies do now: a non zero size, out of the tab order, taking part in hit testing. The Safari cases keep their existing expectations. Five existing tests are adjusted: `focus and disconnection with delaying blur in iOS` now runs with autofill off and expects the deferred close, `Moves the focus across input elements` uses a distinct config for its second field, and `multiTextField Autofill: setClient, setEditingState, show, setSizeAndTransform setEditingState, clearClient`, `form wakeUp and goDormant` and `Validate single element form` gain assertions for the clustering, the parking, the marker class and `aria-hidden`.
- `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/test/engine/platform_dispatcher/view_focus_binding_test.dart`: 5 added, existing tests unchanged. The existing ones passing unmodified is the check that ordinary view unfocus is untouched. The added ones cover a manager stepping between two fields, which is not reported, a focus that never comes back, which still is, and three cases reported at once: an input outside any form, a form that is not the engine's, and a blur to an element outside the view.
- `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/test/engine/pointer_binding/event_position_helper_test.dart`: 1 added, for the pointer position on a non focused proxy.
- `packages/flutter/test/services/autofill_test.dart`: 1 added, for the last connection fallback.

items.body:
Fixes #189744

**Problem**
On iOS 27, long-press-dragging the selection caret in a Web TextField dismisses the keyboard mid-gesture. WebKit transiently blurs the hidden input with a null relatedTarget while the document keeps focus, then refocuses it a frame later,and the engine reacted to that blink on two listeners that each tore the input down. A plain input ignores the same blur, so the cause is Flutter's reaction, not a WebKit limitation.

**Fix**
On iOS both listeners now defer their teardown by 100ms and cancel it if the input refocuses, mirroring the existing #155265 deferred close. Done and tap-away never refocus so they still close, and the deferral is narrowed to the exact drag signature so every other focus transition is unaffected.

**Demo**
Before: https://flutter-demo-52-before.web.app  (keyboard dismisses mid caret drag)
After:  https://flutter-demo-52-after.web.app   (keyboard stays up)

Repro on iOS 27 Safari: tap the field to raise the keyboard, then long-press and drag the selection caret. Before dismisses; after stays up. Done and tap-away still dismiss.

items.body:
Internal: b/144488201

To reproduce:

1. Run `webview_flutter/example`.
2. Tap into a text field. Observe that the keyboard is shown as expected.
3. Tap anywhere else on the screen.

Expected: Keyboard minimizes.
Actual: Keyboard persists.

Haven't tested this on iOS, but this reproduces on all versions of Android. This means that it should be unrelated to any of the `ThreadedInputProxyAdapterView` logic and may be a deeper problem with the platform views. The keyboard also appears to switch from the text field's `InputConnection`. If there's any text typed in the field the suggestion bar will lose it, and it will switch from title to lower case.

See the reproduction also in flutter/flutter#36250.

(/cc @amirh)

To make sure that Flutter can always bring up the keyboard I made the window of virtual display's presentation non focusable.
As a result the embedded Android views cannot bring up the keyboard.

We should figure out if there's some window trickery we can do to let the unfocused window bring up the keyboard. Alternatively see if it's possible to dynamically select the focused window when delivering input events.
